subject: Post-call: BrightCart pilot — SLOs, load shape & throughput confirmation
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: BrightCart pilot — SLOs, load shape & throughput confirmation

Sam — thanks for taking the time today. Quick written recap to make sure we’re aligned before the sizing workshop. I’ve attached a draft SLO matrix and a telemetry checklist to the thread.

Summary from our call (please correct anything I got wrong):
- Primary goal: 95th percentile latency <= 800ms for single-turn search/generation flows; interactive median target ~150ms for snippet responses.
- Steady-state QPS: ~120 QPS (search/generation mix).
- Peak behavior: short crests up to ~650 QPS for 5-10 minutes (marketing promotions).
- Streaming: multi-turn chat sessions expected — ~350-400 concurrent streaming sessions at peak, average token emission ~25 tokens/sec per active session.
- Typical prompt size: 30–80 tokens; average response length forecasted ~220 tokens.
- Availability requirement: production pilot should be in US region; enterprise SLA to be discussed during contracting.

Open questions we flagged on the call:
1) Can you confirm the percent of traffic that is streaming vs non-streaming (rough split)?
2) Do you have sample payload sizes (avg characters / tokens) for user messages and system prompts?
3) Any constraints on burst handling (budget for overage vs capacity reservation)?

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa and Karthik to run a quick sizing sketch based on the numbers above and return GPU/instance ballpark and an ops pattern (caching, batching, fallback).
- We schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop this week to review traffic traces and validate the model choices.
- BrightCart to share 24–72 hours of anonymized request logs (if possible) + expected growth profile.

Attachments: BrightCart_SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx, BrightCart_telemetry_checklist.pdf

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightCart pilot — SLOs, load shape & throughput confirmation

Tessa — thanks for the recap, looks good. A few clarifications from our side:
- Streaming vs non-streaming split: roughly 60% non-streaming (search/generate), 40% streaming/chat during peak windows.
- Payloads: average user message ~40 tokens, system prompts (product+context) add ~110 tokens on average.
- Growth profile: we anticipate 10–15% week-over-week growth during the first 8 weeks of the pilot.
- Burst handling: we prefer a reserved baseline with the ability to burst; can you provide a cost comparison (reserved + burst vs fully reserved) as part of the sizing output?

One important constraint: any pilot deployment must keep data residency in the US and not go to any EU region.

We’ll work on redacting and packaging 48 hours of request logs — should be able to share by EOD tomorrow. Also, can you confirm whether you’d recommend GPU-backed streaming with KV caching for multi-turn sessions vs a higher-concurrency CPU-backed option?

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: BrightCart pilot — SLOs, load shape & throughput confirmation

Sam — great details, that helps. Quick sizing sketch and operational notes below (high level; will refine in the workshop once we have logs):

Assumptions used for sketch:
- Average request: 150 tokens consumed+generated (30 tokens in, 120 tokens out)
- Average token emission for streaming sessions: 25 tokens/sec as Tessa noted
- Peak active streaming sessions: 400 (concurrent)
- Steady QPS non-streaming: 120 QPS
- Peak QPS (brief crest): 650 QPS

Sizing/behavioral suggestions:
1) Dedicated GPU pool recommended for pilot to guarantee p95 latency targets during peaks. Based on our perf curves: a single A100-like GPU (quantized/layer-optimized) can sustain ~200–300 effective QPS for short responses (non-streaming, 120–200 token responses) with batching; streaming sessions are single-request long-lived connections and consume KV state — estimate ~80–120 concurrent streams per GPU depending on model/quantization.
2) Initial pilot baseline: 3–4 GPUs reserved to handle steady-state + small burst buffer, plus autoscale policy to add GPUs when crest > ~350 QPS sustained > 60s. That will cover 120 steady QPS and short crests up to ~650 with autoscale.
3) Streaming plan: isolate streaming pool (or soft-partition streaming traffic on the same pool with lower batching) — recommend reserving 3 GPUs for streaming if BrightCart expects sustained 350–400 concurrent streams; otherwise use 2 GPUs + autoscale.
4) Caching: prefix/KV caching for frequent system prompts saves CPU and tokens on repeated contexts. We should instrument cache hit rate in the pilot telemetry.
5) Observability: must capture per-request token counts, per-stream active duration, and p50/p95/p99 latencies (token and request-level). The attached sample-kpi.json contains suggested telemetry events and thresholds.

Questions for the sizing workshop (to bring samples for):
- Typical distribution of response length (percentiles).
- Fraction of requests that involve long context (>1024 tokens).
- Any rate limits at the client side (e.g., per-user concurrency caps).

I’ll follow up with a quick ballpark resource/cost comparison (reserved 3–4 GPUs + burst vs fully reserved 6 GPUs) and include expected p95 latency ranges per scenario.

Attachment: sample-kpi.json

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
